title: Fraction collection of bioactive compounds from ion chromatography: No longer mission impossible
author: Yates, Carter, et al.
materials: Chromatographic separation was completed on a ThermoFisher Dionex ICS-6000 Ion Chromatograph (details above). The sample solution (4 µL) was cooled to 16 °C prior to injection onto a 2 mm CarboPac PA210 column (30 × 2 mm, 4 um, ThermoFisher catalogue no. 088956) fitted with a 2 mm CarboPac PA210 guard column (30 × 2 mm, 4 um, ThermoFisher catalogue no. 088956). The mobile phase used was a mixture of ultra-pure water and autogenerated potassium hydroxide (KOH) (Table 1). A ThermoFisher Dionex ADRS suppressor, operating at 20 °C and 40 mA, was used to neutralize the mobile phase. Neutralization occurred using the external water source mode of the AXP pump at the rate of 0.25 mL/min.Table 1IC gradient program for collection of fraction with retention time of 15 min.Table 1Time (min)KOH Concentration (mM)Diverter valve (position)Program012BAnalysis12.512ADivert to collection1812ADivert from collection3412B34.1100BCleaning59100B59.112BEquilibration7912B

A length of red PEEK tubing (0.005 inch internal diameter) connected the valve and a centrifuge tube within the block of the Thermomixer (Eppendorf catalogue no. 5382000066 and 5365000028). The block was set to 1 °C, which resulted in an average temperature across the block of 5 °C. A calibrated data logger was present in the block for the duration of the collection.

A sample for 1H NMR analysis was prepared by dissolving the isolated solid in 500 µL of D2O (Sigma catalogue no. 151882) and transferring the resulting solution to a 5 mm diameter NMR tube (Sigma catalogue no. Z565229). The 1H NMR spectrum was acquired at ambient temperature and pressure on a Bruker Avance 500 MHz spectrometer. A zg45 pulse sequence was used with 64 scans and a spectral width of 6.5 ppm was applied. Chemical shifts were expressed in ppm and the NMR spectrum was referenced to residual protonated solvent signal (δ 4.79 ppm) using Mnova software (Mestrelab Research).

steps.title: Prepare honey sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.3 g of stingless bee honey into a 50 mL centrifuge tube, add 30 mL ultra‑pure water (<18.2 MΩ), and shake with a Heathrow Scientific HS120240 shaker until fully dissolved. Centrifuge the mixture at 10 000 g, 4 °C for 10 min. Collect the supernatant and dilute it 1:10 with ultra‑pure water, then transfer the diluted supernatant to amber sample vials.

steps.title: Determine analyte retention time
steps.instruction: Inject a 4 µL aliquot of the prepared honey supernatant (cooled to 16 °C) onto the IC system to obtain a preliminary chromatogram and record the retention time of the target analyte (trehalulose).

steps.title: Set up ion chromatography method
steps.instruction: Configure the ThermoFisher Dionex ICS‑6000 IC with a 2 mm CarboPac PA210 column (30 × 2 mm, 4 µm, catalogue 088956) and matching guard column. Use a mobile phase of ultra‑pure water mixed with autogenerated KOH. Set the Dionex ADRS suppressor to 20 °C and 40 mA, and run the external‑water‑source mode of the AXP pump at 0.25 mL/min. Program the gradient as follows (Time min – KOH mM – Valve): 0 – 12 – B; 12.5 – 12 – A (divert to collection); 18 – 12 – A (divert from collection); 34 – 12 – B; 34.1 – 100 – B (cleaning); 59 – 100 – B; 59.1 – 12 – B (equilibration); 79 – 12 – B.

steps.title: Assemble tubing and set block temperature
steps.instruction: Connect a length of red PEEK tubing (0.005 in ID) between the IC diverter valve and a centrifuge collection tube placed inside the block of an Eppendorf Thermomixer (catalogue 5382000066 and 5365000028). Set the block temperature to 1 °C (average block temperature ≈ 5 °C) and keep a calibrated data logger in the block for the duration of the collection.

steps.title: Collect fractions and swap tubes
steps.instruction: Perform successive IC injections of the honey sample; each injection yields ~3 mL of fractionate containing ~8 mg L⁻¹ trehalulose. When the collection tube reaches ~40 mL (≈ 13 injections), manually replace it with an empty tube and freeze the full tube. Repeat until three 50 mL centrifuge tubes of fractionate have been collected.

steps.title: Lyophilize fractions and combine
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry the three frozen 50 mL tubes in a Christ Alpha 1–4 LSC with Lyocube 4–8 for 18 h at 0.5 mbar. Wash the resulting dried material with small aliquots of pure water and combine all washes into a 15 mL centrifuge tube. Freeze this tube and lyophilize again using the same program, yielding approximately two sugar crystals (< 1 mg).

steps.title: Prepare NMR sample
steps.instruction: Dissolve the isolated solid in 500 µL D₂O (Sigma catalogue 151882) and transfer the solution to a 5 mm NMR tube (Sigma catalogue Z565229).

steps.title: Acquire 1H NMR spectrum
steps.instruction: Record a ¹H NMR spectrum at ambient temperature and pressure on a Bruker Avance 500 MHz spectrometer using a zg45 pulse sequence, 64 scans, and a spectral width of 6.5 ppm. Reference chemical shifts to the residual solvent signal at δ 4.79 ppm with Mnova software (Mestrelab Research).

steps.title: Confirm identity by chromatogram and NMR comparison
steps.instruction: Compare the IC/PAD chromatogram of the isolated fraction with a standard solution containing glucose, sucrose, fructose, trehalulose, and erlose. Then compare the ¹H NMR spectrum of the isolated compound with that of a trehalulose standard; confirmation of trehalulose is achieved when both chromatographic and NMR profiles match the standards.
